topic: Ionization of Water and the pH Scale
title: Kw and the pH Scale Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Lemon juice tastes sour, milk tastes mild and an antacid tastes bitter, yet all three are mostly water. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya squeezes a lemon in her kitchen and we find out that even pure water is never just water.

You will see water molecules pass a proton on the molecule bench to make hydronium and hydroxide ions, only about 2 in every billion at a time. We build the ionic product of water, Kw = [H3O+][OH-] = 1.0 x 10^-14 at 298 K, define pH and pOH step by step, prove pH + pOH = 14, and read real values on the pH scale (lemon juice 2.2, milk 6.8, blood 7.4, milk of magnesia about 10). Then a pause-and-think check, NCERT's soft drink example (pH 2.42), the 10^-8 M HCl trap (pH 6.98, not 8), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 66 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
